text:
Tomáš Novák: Quick q from the us-west degradation that’s been dragging on — what’s the expected cadence for status page updates when there’s *no new info*? We keep putting “Next update in 30 min” and then it’s basically “still investigating” for 2 hours.

Rafael Mendes: yeah this is the pattern we’re trying to fix. customers read “next update” as a commitment, not “we’ll remember to look at it again”

Christine Wong: +1. and support is getting pinged every time we miss the time by a few mins.

Sean Gallagher: we need something simple for oncall:
- commit to a next update time you can actually hit
- if there’s no material change, post a short “no significant change” but still confirm we’re engaged + what we’re doing
- don’t keep a 30m cadence for 6 hours unless it’s a Sev0/1 with ongoing impact + lots of movement

Tomáš Novák: ok but what’s “simple” here — is it severity based? also we’re getting tripped up by the absolute time vs “in 30 min” thing.

Kira Thompson: status page UI shows “Next update” as an absolute timestamp in the incident entry (it’s not super obvious in the editor). If we keep writing “in 30 min” in the body, customers will still ask “30 min from when?”

Devon Price: incident-bot change (in review) is going to prompt for `next_update_at` explicitly. We can nudge to use absolute like “Next update by 19:00 UTC” and the bot can render that consistently.

Aisha Bello: from a metrics angle, “time-to-first-update” is easy; “update timeliness” is going to be measured against the promised next_update time. so we want that field to be meaningful.

Tomáš Novák: so guidance should be “always put next update as absolute time (UTC)”?

Rafael Mendes: yes please. internal can be local, external should be UTC. support + customers are global.

Christine Wong: + we should avoid being overly precise when we don’t know. e.g. “Next update in 30 minutes” implies we expect meaningful progress in 30 min.

Sean Gallagher: proposed rules of thumb (for runbook):
- Sev1: every 30 min until Identified. once Identified + mitigation in progress, every 60 min is fine if stable.
- Sev2: every 60–120 min depending on churn.
- Monitoring: can stretch to 2–4 hours *but* still include a next update time if we’re keeping the incident open.

Tomáš Novák: what about “next update sooner if we learn more”? can we say that without it sounding like a cop-out?

Kira Thompson: we can standardize it as a clause:
“Next update by 19:00 UTC, or sooner if we have additional information.”
That reads like a commitment + acknowledges uncertainty.

Devon Price: fwiw bot can also block “Next update: TBD” unless it’s the initial Investigating update. (guardrail idea)

Rafael Mendes: pls yes. “TBD” becomes “never” in long incidents.

Tomáš Novák: edge case: shift change. if i set next update for 19:00 UTC but I’m handing off at 18:30, is that ok?

Sean Gallagher: ok as long as handoff includes the commitment. new oncall owns hitting it.

Talia Benson: jumping in — this is exactly the confusion we heard in training feedback. can we align on a single sentence for oncall:
“If you can’t reasonably provide new info, don’t promise a short next-update. Set a realistic time and use the ‘no significant change’ template if needed.”

Christine Wong: + “no significant change” still needs *something*: what’s impacted + what customers can do (retry/backoff, region pinning, fallback models) + what we’re doing. otherwise it reads like spam.

Aisha Bello: also for long-running degraded perf, customers mostly want: is this my region/model? and is there a workaround? so if we don’t have new root cause, we can at least tighten the scope each update.

Tomáš Novák: ok so if the only update is “we’re still seeing elevated 5xx in us-west streaming; mitigation is still rolling out; next update by X” — that’s acceptable.

Rafael Mendes: yep.

Incident Bot: Reminder: This incident has a status page update SLA. Please add a next update time and publish an update if overdue. (Triggered at T+60m)

Tomáš Novák: lol the bot is already yelling at us.

Devon Price: that reminder threshold is currently hardcoded at 60m in staging. we can make it severity-aware once we have severity mapped.

Sean Gallagher: action items:
1) Tomáš/Kira update runbook section w/ severity-based cadence + “Next update by <TIME> UTC” guidance
2) Devon: bot prompt should default to UTC display, accept local input, and include the “or sooner” clause as optional toggle
3) Rafael/Christine: review with Support if 2h cadence in Monitoring is ok for customer expectations

Kira Thompson: I’ll draft wording today and drop in #docs for quick review.

Tomáš Novák: thanks all. I’ll also add an example scenario: long-running partial degradation w/ stable mitigation rollout + how to adjust next-update over time.

Rafael Mendes: :thumbsup: and let’s be consistent: if we miss the next_update, we update immediately and set a new one. no silent misses.
